Patch to allow `/var/tmp` as PID file location for pasta at https://archives.passt.top/passt-dev/20260925205946.1980078-1-sbrivio@redhat.com/.

Debian sid packages with updated AppArmor policy now available for [amd64](http://ftp.debian.org/debian/pool/main/p/passt/passt_0.0~git20260925.df90211-1_amd64.deb) and [arm64](http://ftp.debian.org/debian/pool/main/p/passt/passt_0.0~git20260925.df90211-1_arm64.deb).
dropped the workaround, only Debian-sid tests are failing (as expected): https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29823

I did not have a proper look here yet so I might have missed something but do we need the pid at all to move the cgroup? Like could we not just start the main pasta process in the right cgroup from the start and not move after start?
Like the SysProcAttr from the go exec command has
```
	UseCgroupFD                bool      // Whether to make use of the CgroupFD field.
	CgroupFD                   int       // File descriptor of a cgroup to put the new process into.
```

Second do we need to write a tmpfile to persistent disk? Could we pass a pipe fd instead an avoid the whole file might leak thing for each start.

> I did not have a proper look here yet so I might have missed something but do we need the pid at all to move the cgroup? Like could we not just start the main pasta process in the right cgroup from the start and not move after start? Like the SysProcAttr from the go exec command has

I know about that feature but I don't see how we can use it here as we have a ordering problem.  When we create the network namespace and run pasta there is no cgroup yet as the cgroup is created later once we have a conmon process.  IMO the conmon process should still be the main process for the scope.

> Second do we need to write a tmpfile to persistent disk? Could we pass a pipe fd instead an avoid the whole file might leak thing for each start.

that is not permitted by pasta now, since it uses `O_CREAT|O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC` and that fails with an already opened pipe fd.

> we have a ordering problem. When we create the network namespace and run pasta there is no cgroup yet as the cgroup is created later once we have a conmon process. IMO the conmon process should still be the main process for the scope.

I have realized I know way too little to have an opinion on the overall process, and I must let this be reviewed by more familiar maintainers.
